blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—Prosecutors at the International Criminal Court (ICC) are proposing to remove nearly 7,000 items from their massive trove of evidence in the crimes against humanity case against former President Rodrigo Duterte. The proposed cuts to the list of evidence stem from the prosecution’s restructuring and review of the material it intends to present at trial. So far, the prosecution said it has removed 253 items. In an Oct. 6 submission made public only early Tuesday, the prosecution said it had classified the evidence into seven categories for use in the trial, which is scheduled to begin on Nov. 30.
